match.reason: The closest bank point, Gradient of an interval, covers rise over run and the positive and negative cases, but it does not teach the zero gradient of a flat line or the undefined gradient of a vertical line that the new point requires, so it is narrower than the brief.

draft.title: Gradient of a line
card: Gradient measures how steep a line is. Gradient \(=\) rise \(\div\) run. The rise is the vertical change and the run is the horizontal change between two points.
From \((1, 2)\) to \((4, 8)\), the rise is \(8 - 2 = 6\) and the run is \(4 - 1 = 3\). The gradient is \(\frac{6}{3} = 2\).
A line going up to the right has a positive gradient. A line going down to the right has a negative gradient.
A flat line has gradient \(0\), because its rise is \(0\). A vertical line has an undefined gradient, because its run is \(0\) and we cannot divide by \(0\).

2.alt: A straight line going up to the right through the points (1, 2) and (4, 8). Between them the rise is 6 and the run is 3.

draft.remember: Rise over run: down is negative, flat is zero, vertical is undefined.

a.q: What is the gradient of the line through \((2, 7)\) and \((5, 1)\)?
a.why: The rise is \(1 - 7 = -6\) and the run is \(5 - 2 = 3\), so the gradient is \(\frac{-6}{3} = -2\). Using run over rise gives \(-\frac{1}{2}\), which turns the fraction upside down.
a.clue: The line goes down to the right. Put the rise on top.

b.q: Two posts on a map grid are at \((3, -2)\) and \((3, 5)\). What is the gradient of the line through them?
b.why: Both points have \(x = 3\), so the run is \(0\) and the line is vertical. Dividing the rise of \(7\) by a run of \(0\) cannot be done, so the gradient is undefined. Zero is the gradient of a flat line, where the rise is \(0\).
b.clue: Compare the two x values. What is the run?
